displayDescription: Paper cards hop from a stack beside a glowing bulb onto a pinboard, get pinned and connected by thread on a slate desk at dusk.
styleRenderer: Three.js 0.186.1 WebGLRenderer (local node_modules, bundled with esbuild into scene.bundle.js): procedural tabletop set, MeshStandardMaterial paper/felt/brass/glass, fixed SpotLight key with PCF soft shadow maps for contact shadows, hemisphere fill
Canvas 2D (load-time procedural textures: felt dot weave, paper fibre with printed rules, bulb halo)
HTML/CSS overlay for title copy and stationary vignette
motionEngine: GSAP 3 (local gsap.min.js): one paused timeline, built in scene.bundle.js and registered inline in index.html as window.__timelines["video"], owns all proxy values (card hop progress, landing rock, pin drop, thread draw length, bulb glow, title opacity), with held 15 fps exposure easing; Three.js redraws from those values on timeline update and on hf-seek
audioDescription: Silent preview: no audio track, music, effects or voice.
limitations: Digital simulation of photographed object animation: rendered in Three.js, not photographed, and Pillow frame normalisation does not apply.
Blender was not used, at the user's request.

Materials are approximate: the glass bulb is a transparent standard material with an additive halo, not refractive transmission. The paper, felt and brass use procedural textures, and the threads are tube meshes.
The 15 fps held exposures imitate stop-motion cadence. The motion is not physically simulated.

No named preview recipe exists in STYLE.json, so this refresh shows the source-frame lessons: hopping, tilting object characters with contact shadows, a fixed camera and light, and a scene-dependent cool slate dusk background instead of the earlier cream canvas.
Not rendered or browser-tested by the agent; host QA is pending.
